findings.comment: If manualTests.txt does not exist yet (e.g., on a clean clone before any manual tests are created), fs.readFileSync will throw an unhandled ENOENT error and crash the script.

makeManual.mts populates manualTests.txt using the filename in genDir (e.g., foo_test.go), but this check looks up the capitalized base name testName (e.g., Foo). Because of this format mismatch, manualTests.has(testName) will evaluate to false and the test will not be skipped.

There is a mismatch in how test files are named on disk and how test names are recorded for skipping in convertFourslash.mts. In convertFourslash.mts, generated files are named `${test.name}_test.go`, and tests are skipped if manualTests contains `test.name[0].toUpperCase() + test.name.substring(1)`. In this script, if the user passes `foo` (as shown in the PR description `npm run manualtest testname`), `genTestFile` checks for `genDir/foo` instead of `foo_test.go` and exits with an error. If the user passes `foo_test.go`, `foo_test.go` is written to `manualTests.txt`, but convertFourslash.mts will check for `Foo` (capitalized and without `_test.go`), causing convertFourslash to regenerate the file anyway.
When no arguments are supplied, the script exits without printing usage instructions or an error message.
